source: Independently authored practice items based on the user-provided study guide. They are not actual Adobe exam questions.

questions.question: A team wants to show different content to defined audience segments but does not need a statistical comparison between those experiences. Which activity type best fits?

options.text: A/B test
Experience Targeting
Multivariate test
Auto-Allocate

questions.explanation: Experience Targeting presents experiences to qualifying segments. A/B and multivariate activities are experiments, while Auto-Allocate shifts traffic within a test.

incorrectExplanations.A: A/B testing compares outcomes across experiences.
incorrectExplanations.C: A multivariate test evaluates combinations of changes.
incorrectExplanations.D: Auto-Allocate optimizes traffic among test experiences.

questions.question: Observed traffic allocation differs substantially from the configured split in an otherwise active experiment. What should the team investigate first?

options.text: Sample ratio mismatch and delivery or implementation behavior
The activity's business hypothesis wording
The recommendation catalog
Whether the test has reached statistical significance

questions.explanation: A gap between configured and observed allocation is a sample ratio mismatch. Investigate implementation and delivery before interpreting outcomes.

incorrectExplanations.B: Hypothesis wording does not usually explain an observed traffic split.
incorrectExplanations.C: Catalog configuration is unrelated unless this is specifically a recommendations issue.
incorrectExplanations.D: Significance concerns outcome confidence, not whether visitors were assigned as expected.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Analytics for Target (A4T)?

options.text: Replace the Target delivery engine with Analytics
Report Target activity and experience data in Adobe Analytics
Automatically render AEM components
Create every Target audience without activation

questions.explanation: A4T makes Target activity and experience data available for Analytics reporting. It does not replace Target delivery or automatically render AEM content.

incorrectExplanations.A: Target remains responsible for its delivery decisions.
incorrectExplanations.C: AEM rendering requires its own configured integration.
incorrectExplanations.D: Audience creation and activation are separate concerns.

questions.question: Why should teams validate Target changes in staging before production rollout?

options.text: To increase the activity's traffic allocation
To test changes before they affect live visitors
To eliminate the need for audiences
To avoid documenting the activity

questions.explanation: Environment separation enables a controlled check of implementation and experience behavior before production visitors are affected.

incorrectExplanations.A: Staging does not inherently change production traffic allocation.
incorrectExplanations.C: Audiences may still be part of the activity design.
incorrectExplanations.D: Documentation remains important in every environment.

questions.question: A decision must be available before above-the-fold content is rendered to minimize browser-side flicker. Which approach most directly addresses that requirement?

options.text: Server-side delivery with the decision made before rendering
Client-side tags that run after the page is painted
Email personalization at send time
Remove the default experience

questions.explanation: A server-side decision can be incorporated before the page is rendered, avoiding the client-side swap that causes flicker.

incorrectExplanations.B: Applying a client-side offer after paint can create visible flicker.
incorrectExplanations.C: Email delivery is unrelated to page rendering.
incorrectExplanations.D: Removing the default does not ensure a timely decision or reliable fallback.

questions.question: A recommendations request returns no eligible items for every visitor. What is the best first investigation?

options.text: Increase the activity's traffic allocation
Review criteria restrictions and catalog item data
Rename the page mbox
Replace the algorithm without checking inputs

questions.explanation: Overly restrictive criteria or missing, stale, or ineligible catalog items commonly explain empty recommendations.

incorrectExplanations.A: Traffic allocation does not make excluded catalog items eligible.
incorrectExplanations.C: A name change is not the first evidence-based check.
incorrectExplanations.D: The catalog and criteria should be validated before changing algorithms.

questions.question: Why does the provided study guide recommend keeping global Target behavior lightweight?

options.text: It can run on every page where the library is loaded, so extra work affects many pages
It cannot return offers
It is only available to mobile applications
It replaces page-specific requests in every implementation

questions.explanation: The guide describes the global request as running on pages with the library; keeping it lightweight limits cost across the site. Verify current behavior in Adobe documentation.

incorrectExplanations.B: The guide does not state that global behavior cannot return offers.
incorrectExplanations.C: The concept is described for pages where the web library is loaded.
incorrectExplanations.D: The guide recommends page-specific requests for page-level experiences.

questions.verification: The exact global mbox behavior and naming are marked for current-documentation verification.

questions.question: A customer can refresh the order confirmation page. What measurement risk should the implementation guard against?

options.text: Duplicate conversion or revenue counting
An automatic change to audience membership
A lower recommendation catalog quality score
A change to the test's configured traffic split

questions.explanation: If order confirmation logic fires again on refresh or back navigation, conversion and revenue can be duplicated.

incorrectExplanations.B: Page refresh does not inherently alter audience membership.
incorrectExplanations.C: Order-event firing is separate from catalog quality.
incorrectExplanations.D: Duplicate conversion events do not directly reconfigure traffic allocation.

questions.question: Staging sends a Target request, but production sends none. Which set of checks should come first?

options.text: Production library and tag loading, consent state, and script blocking
Recommendations ranking strategy
Analytics attribution window only
The activity's statistical significance

questions.explanation: No request points first to delivery: verify that production loads the library and tag and that consent, blocking, or script errors are not preventing the request.

incorrectExplanations.B: Ranking strategy cannot explain a request that never fires.
incorrectExplanations.C: Attribution does not control whether a request is sent.
incorrectExplanations.D: Significance is evaluated after eligible traffic and outcomes are collected.

questions.question: A request fires, but the expected experience is not returned. Which checks are appropriate next steps? Select all that apply.

options.text: Confirm the activity is live and within its scheduled dates
Check audience qualification and traffic allocation
Check whether the offer is active and correctly mapped
Change the page font before inspecting the response

questions.explanation: Once delivery is confirmed, check activity status and dates, audience qualification, allocation, and offer configuration. These checks cover common reasons for a missing experience.

incorrectExplanations.D: Font styling is unrelated to whether Target returns the offer; inspect request and response evidence first.

questions.question: A retailer needs private logged-in pricing decided before rendering but also wants inexpensive client-side tests for non-sensitive layout changes. Which design is most suitable?

options.text: Use client-side delivery for all decisions, including pricing
Use a hybrid design and keep visitor identity consistent across delivery paths
Use email delivery for both page experiences
Place every decision in the global mbox

questions.explanation: A hybrid design can use server-side delivery for the pricing decision and client-side delivery for simpler layout tests. Shared identity helps keep decisions consistent.

incorrectExplanations.A: Client-only delivery does not meet the stated before-render requirement.
incorrectExplanations.C: Email delivery does not personalize the live page.
incorrectExplanations.D: The guide advises keeping global behavior lightweight rather than putting every decision there.

questions.question: Target conversions are higher than Analytics orders for the same reporting period. What should the team compare before changing the activity?

options.text: Attribution windows, deduplication, identity, and time zones
The recommendations catalog's image URLs
The activity's name only
Whether to remove all conversion metrics

questions.explanation: Differences in attribution, deduplication, identity, and time-zone handling can lead systems to report different conversion totals.

incorrectExplanations.B: Catalog image URLs do not explain conversion reporting differences.
incorrectExplanations.C: Renaming an activity does not align measurement definitions.
incorrectExplanations.D: Removing metrics hides the discrepancy rather than diagnosing it.
